field.label: Enable Xray Client
field.help: Enable or disable the Xray client service.

field.label: Show Expert Config Tab
field.help: Show an extra "Expert Config" tab with the exact /usr/local/etc/xray/config.json Xray is running (or would run). This is all Advanced Mode controls: the advanced fields in the dialogs are governed separately by their own "Show advanced fields" / "Show additional conditions" checkboxes. The Configuration Mode selector (UI Builder or Raw JSON) is on that tab. You can view the tab read-only or edit it manually; saving there switches the plugin to Raw JSON mode, and the config is validated with xray run -test before it is applied.

field.label: Log Level
field.help: Logging verbosity for Xray-core.

field.label: Enable Access Log
field.help: Write every proxied connection to /var/log/xray/access.log. Off by default: with the TUN inbound all network traffic is logged and the file grows without rotation. Enable only while debugging, and clear it from VPN → Xray Client → Access Log afterwards.

field.label: Enable DNS Log
field.help: Log every DNS query the built-in DNS server handles (domain, matched server, result) — invaluable when a domain silently fails to resolve. Off by default.

field.label: Mask IP Addresses in Logs
field.hint: off, or a CIDR such as 10.0.0.0/8
field.help: A CIDR range, e.g. 10.0.0.0/8 — the matching octets are masked in Xray's logs (e.g. 192.168.1.200 → 192.168.x.x). Useful when sharing logs without leaking your LAN or client addresses.

field.label: Enable Native TUN Inbound
field.help: Xray creates the interface itself while the service runs (it does not exist otherwise). Enable this, Apply, then assign it under Interfaces -> Assignments.

field.label: TUN Interface Name
field.help: System interface name Xray creates for the TUN inbound. Must start with "tun_" (default: tun_xray0): OPNsense only recognises TUN interfaces with that prefix, so Xray would create one that never shows up in Interfaces -> Assignments otherwise. 5-15 characters. Visible in Interfaces -> Assignments while Xray is running.

field.label: TUN Tunnel Subnet
field.help: Gateway prefix for the TUN inbound (default: 10.255.0.1/30, CIDR 1..31). Xray keeps the gateway address for itself as the in-tunnel endpoint and assigns the next address to the interface (10.255.0.2 for a /30). Route traffic to the gateway via an assigned gateway + policy rule.

field.label: TUN MTU
field.help: Maximum Transmission Unit for the TUN interface (default: 1500).

field.label: TUN IPv6 Subnet (fd00::/64)
field.help: Unique-local IPv6 prefix for the TUN, e.g. fd00::1/64. On FreeBSD Xray assigns link-local IPv6 automatically (derived from the IPv4 address) and this field is parsed but unused; on Linux it assigns the IPv6 local address to the interface. Leave empty to disable IPv6 on the TUN (default).

field.label: Outbound Interface Binding
field.help: Empty = off (default). «auto» or an interface name (e.g. vmx1) binds every outbound socket, so Xray's own traffic can never loop back through the TUN. WINDOWS + LINUX + MACOS work out of the box; on FREEBSD Xray needs a second routing table: add net.fibs=2 to /boot/loader.conf and REBOOT the firewall first — with net.fibs=1 Xray will refuse to start and Apply will be rejected.

field.label: Enable Local SOCKS5 Proxy
field.help: Enable local SOCKS5 inbound (with UDP support) for apps and healthchecks.

field.label: SOCKS5 Authentication
field.help: noauth — open access (safe only on 127.0.0.1 or with a firewall limiting the port); password — require the username and password below.

field.label: SOCKS5 Username
field.help: Username for SOCKS5 authentication. Required when authentication is set to password.

field.label: SOCKS5 Password
field.help: Password for SOCKS5 authentication. Required when authentication is set to password.

field.label: SOCKS5 Listen IP Address
field.help: IP to bind local SOCKS5 proxy (use 127.0.0.1 for local only, or 0.0.0.0 / LAN IP for LAN devices). When binding to LAN you should also enable SOCKS5 authentication and restrict access with firewall rules.

field.label: SOCKS5 Port
field.help: Port for SOCKS5 inbound (default: 10808).

field.label: Enable Local HTTP Proxy
field.help: Enable local HTTP proxy inbound.

field.label: HTTP Proxy Listen IP Address
field.help: IP to bind the HTTP proxy. Leave empty to reuse the SOCKS5 listen address.

field.label: HTTP Proxy Authentication
field.help: noauth — open access (safe only on 127.0.0.1 or with a firewall limiting the port); password — require the username and password below (clients must send Proxy-Authorization).

field.label: HTTP Proxy Username
field.help: Username for HTTP proxy authentication. Required when authentication is set to password.

field.label: HTTP Proxy Password
field.help: Password for HTTP proxy authentication. Required when authentication is set to password.

field.label: HTTP Port
field.help: Port for HTTP proxy inbound (default: 10809).

field.label: Internal gRPC Stats API Port
field.help: Local loopback port used by the plugin to query live traffic counters from Xray (default: 10085).

field.label: Enable Automatic Latency & Traffic Polling
field.help: When enabled, the Outbound Nodes table refreshes traffic automatically at the interval below, and latency every 5 minutes on a separate timer, without clicking the button.

field.label: Traffic Polling Interval (seconds)
field.help: How often to fetch traffic counters in the background (30-3600 seconds, default 60). Latency is polled every 5 minutes independently. The «Live» switch above the Outbound Nodes table has its own 5-second interval and is not affected by this value.
